mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce discount rates for equity valuations and stimulate economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 5.0% signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and dampens equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and fall in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong economic expansion with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2pp and UNRATE falls > 0.1pp in 3 months
failure_condition: The joint condition (FEDFUNDS rising >0.2pp and UNRATE falling >0.1pp) occurs in more than 50% of cases but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals improving labor market conditions and rising corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when UNRATE > 5.0%, a decline in UNRATE > 0.1pp is followed by negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as tight labor markets support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1800.0 thousand units signals weak consumer demand and reduced construction activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1800.0.

mechanism_narrative: In a high GDP growth regime (GDPC1 > 11400.0), a rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL > 205.0) signals potential monetary tightening and reduced real consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when GDPC1 > 11400.0, the condition CPIAUCSL > 205.0 is followed by positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a demand-supply mismatch that may lead to inflationary pressures and reduced corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 0.5% and INDPRO falls > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: The joint condition (HOUST rising >0.5% and INDPRO falling >0.3%) occurs in more than 50% of cases but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of those instances.
